sentencing_structure.consecutive_requirement: Mandatory consecutive to predicate sentence; cannot be made concurrent by court
sentencing_structure.anti_stacking: §1028A(b)(4): multiple §1028A counts from same scheme may run concurrent with each other but still consecutive to predicate

elements: 1. Conviction for an enumerated predicate offense
2. During and in relation to that predicate offense
3. Defendant knowingly (Flores-Figueroa: knowing the ID belongs to a real person)
6. A means of identification of another person
7. Use was 'at the crux' of what makes the conduct criminal (Dubin)

interpretive.rule: 'At the crux' test: §1028A requires identity use to be the central element of the crime, not merely incidental. Overbilling using patient IDs = NOT at the crux. Impersonation, account takeover, fraudulent account opening = at the crux.
Knowledge requirement extends to 'real person' element — defendant must know the means of identification belongs to a real person. Deliberate targeting of a specific individual satisfies this.
interpretive.note: Primary citation lives in §1028 standard; cross-cited here for §1028A knowledge analysis

referral_strategy.note: §1028A is a criminal statute with no private civil right of action. Its value is as a referral lever: presenting a case to FBI/USSS/IRS CI/Treasury IG with §1028A analysis raises the prosecutorial stakes from white-collar-probation range to mandatory-prison territory, which increases the likelihood of prosecution and cooperation agreements.
referral_targets: IRS Criminal Investigation (for tax-related identity use)
